components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The next meaningful action in a study workflow.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A supporting action that stays visually behind the primary path.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { min-height: 44px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; padding: 0 18px; border: 0; border-radius: 10px; background: var(--sheet); color: var(--ink); font-family: var(--font-manrope), Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 750; box-shadow: 0 7px 16px rgba(34, 40, 52, .10); cursor: pointer; transition: transform .18s ease, background .18s ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #f1eee6; transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: translateY(0); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--cobalt); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: The standard field for group, source, and material editing.

components.name: Context Navigation Item
components.description: A labeled location inside the current study group.
components.html: Study library
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 11px; padding: 11px 12px; border-radius: 10px; background: transparent; color: #555f70; font-family: var(--font-manrope), Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 730; text-decoration: none; transition: background .18s ease, color .18s ease, transform .18s ease; } .ds-nav-item:hover, .ds-nav-item-active { color: var(--ink); background: var(--sheet); box-shadow: 0 5px 13px rgba(30, 35, 45, .08); } .ds-nav-item:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--cobalt); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Paper Panel
components.description: A raised working sheet for summaries, editors, and focused study content.
components.html:
CURRENT STACK

components.css: .ds-paper-panel { max-width: 360px; padding: 24px; border-radius: 14px; background: var(--sheet); color: var(--ink); box-shadow: 0 16px 38px rgba(34, 40, 52, .12); font-family: var(--font-manrope), Arial, sans-serif; transition: transform .2s ease; } .ds-paper-panel:hover { transform: translateY(-3px); } .ds-paper-panel:focus-within { outline: 3px solid var(--cobalt); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-paper-panel h3 { margin: 30px 0 8px; font-family: var(--font-fraunces), Georgia, serif; font-size: 25px; font-weight: 650; letter-spacing: -.025em; } .ds-paper-panel p { margin: 0; color: var(--muted); font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.6; } .ds-paper-label { color: var(--cobalt); font-size: 11px; font-weight: 900; letter-spacing: .08em; }

narrative.overview:
StudyStackLM feels like a shared study desk prepared before a focused session: warm paper, precisely ruled sheets, stacked lesson pages, clear tabs, and confident ink. Its editorial asymmetry gives source material and generated study objects distinct physical presence while the interface remains fast to scan and easy to operate.

The visual system makes provenance tangible. Cobalt links actions and citations, coral flags attention and draft states, mint confirms ready or correct states, and ruled lines connect study content to its source. The result should feel academically responsible and encouraging, with the warmth of a notebook and the order of a ledger.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper canvas with brighter working sheets.
Fraunces-led editorial hierarchy paired with compact Manrope controls.
Asymmetric stacks, source tabs, ruled backgrounds, and restrained rotations.
Cobalt actions, coral attention, and mint verification with text or icons reinforcing every state.
Dense study tools framed by quiet margins and one dominant work area.

rules.name: The Ink Economy Rule
rules.body: Use cobalt for action, location, progress, and provenance; coral for attention; mint for verified or correct states. Their meaning depends on restraint.

rules.name: The Evidence Rule
rules.body: Never communicate correctness, error, readiness, or selection through color alone; pair color with direct copy, an icon, a border, or a state label.

rules.name: The Two-Hand Rule
rules.body: Fraunces carries the lesson and the question; Manrope carries the interface around them.

rules.name: The Study-Text Rule
rules.body: Reading surfaces get generous line-height and controlled measure, while controls remain compact and weight-forward.

rules.name: The Quiet Margin Rule
rules.body: Dense controls may sit close together inside the active object, but the active object itself must retain clear space from navigation and neighboring work.

rules.name: The Soft-Lift Rule
rules.body: Raise complete sheets and active navigation; keep lists and controls flat until interaction gives them a reason to move.

rules.name: The Ledger Shape Rule
rules.body: Rounded rectangles should read as sheets, controls, or status labels; do not turn the interface into a field of interchangeable cards.

dos: Do keep source references visible and open them without making the student lose their place.
Do use one dominant work area with supporting columns, quiet margins, and clear row structure.
Do reserve cobalt for action, navigation, progress, and provenance; reserve coral and mint for their established meanings.
Do pair every status color with explicit copy, an icon, a border, or a label.
Do preserve 44px minimum targets, visible focus, keyboard flow, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do use Fraunces for lesson authority and Manrope for operational clarity.
donts: Don't replace the study ledger with a uniform dashboard of interchangeable cards.
Don't add glassy halos, heavy outlines, or decorative shadows that compete with the paper stack.
Don't use coral or mint as arbitrary decoration; their semantic meaning must remain stable.
Don't rotate ordinary panels; rotations belong to literal stacks of lesson or material sheets.
Don't hide navigation labels on mobile or make a state legible only by color.
